sources.entry: aws-s3-uploader - Simple macOS app for uploading files to Amazon Web Services.

summary.one_liner: A simple macOS app that uploads files to Amazon S3 via drag and drop onto a status bar bucket icon or app window.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs as a macOS status bar item and window where you drag files or folders onto a bucket icon to upload them to Amazon Web Services S3. You log in with an AWS access key and secret key, which the app can remember so you don't re-enter them on each start. Upload settings include permissions and storage classes. Clicking an uploaded file in the list gives you its S3 link. The README also says you can edit a `.awscredentials.json` file manually to configure credentials. Dropping many files at once is supported, including directories.
use_cases: upload files to an S3 bucket from a Mac
drag and drop uploads to Amazon S3
get shareable S3 links for uploaded files
set S3 permissions and storage class on uploads
quick file upload from the macOS menu bar
stack: Swift (implied by macOS app; not stated in README)
notable: Lives in the macOS status bar as a bucket icon for drag-and-drop uploads
Remembers AWS login so credentials are not re-entered at each start
Supports dropping multiple files and whole directories
Lets you set permissions and storage classes per upload
Clicking an uploaded file in the list copies or shows its S3 link
caveats: Automatic URL-to-clipboard write and notifications cannot be disabled yet (listed as todo)
No way to abort uploads yet (todo)
No tests and no packaged distribution yet (todo)
